description: ABILITY BASELINE -> kick error on: c1 horizontal (xmm1), c2 vertical (xmm12), c3 power (xmm6) (code cave). WHAT IT DOES: it makes the kick-error CEILING depend on the player. THE PROBLEM, STATED CORRECTLY (this paragraph replaces an earlier, wrong one): the stock game does NOT give an unpressured clean kick zero error. With the five cleanliness-factor functions actually executing (emu_kickerror S11b) a standing, unpressured, zeroed-world kick leaves the builder with h 4.200 deg / v 2.100 deg / p 28.84% - because c1 carries the unconditional kick-class multiply at 0x14401be1e and c2, c3 are DERIVED from c1 (c2 = 0.5*c1 + 0.5 at 0x14401c849; c3 = (0.5*c1 + 0.5) then *0.3 at 0x14401c76a/0x14401c8ce), so the ideal vector c = (1,1,1) is unreachable on 172 of 176 kick ids. The stock game also DOES weight ability, but only on the SIGMA factors (s_i = c_i*(0.5 + 0.5*f)), i.e. on how wide the draw spreads INSIDE that ceiling, never on the ceiling itself. Net effect in stock: the ceiling is IDENTICAL for a 40-rated and a 99-rated player, and the p90 miss on a 20 m ball separates them by only about 2.4x (56 cm vs 23 cm of weight/loft error). A bad player therefore cannot mis-hit an unpressured ball any WORSE than an elite one can - he only does it a bit more often. That is the gap this cave fills: it scales the cleanliness factors themselves by an ability term, so the ceiling moves. At gain 0.3 the same separation becomes about 11.9x, and ability 99 stays bit-identical to stock. MECHANISM: hooks the kick-miss builder 0x14401a900 at 0x14401b3a7 (the 8-byte 'movss xmm3,[rip->4.25f]' sigma-K load), jumps to the 91-byte int3 run at 0x1438b4835, computes S = max(0, min(1, 1 - gain*(1 - f))) where f = the ability factor at [rsp+0x40] (0x143ed71d0: 40 -> 0.0, 60 -> 0.1, 75 -> 0.5, 90 -> 0.9, 99 -> 1.0, and it can exceed 1), multiplies c1 horizontal (xmm1), c2 vertical (xmm12), c3 power (xmm6) by S, re-materialises xmm3 = K from an immediate, and returns to 0x14401b3af. NO memory reads except [rsp+0x40] (which the builder itself re-reads at 0x14401b72f), no calls, no stack use, no memory writes; clobbers only rax/xmm0/xmm2/xmm5, proven dead at the hook, and not even EFLAGS (mov/movd/movaps/subss/mulss/minss/maxss/xorps write no flags). xmm2 and xmm5 do still differ from stock at the builder's ret - they are volatile in the Win64 ABI and the stock builder already leaves garbage in them, so that is harmless, but the earlier wording 'no live register differs' was too strong. The clamp is two-sided and NaN-safe, so f < 0, f = NaN, f = +-inf or a mis-set gain can at worst zero a cleanliness factor (= the game's own full ceiling) and never exceed it. IDENTITY: at f >= 1.0 (ability 99, or anyone whose skill/team bonuses push the effective ability past 99) S is exactly 1.0 and the whole 0x3c-byte kick-miss struct is BIT-IDENTICAL to unpatched - checked both with planted factors and with the factor functions live, at f = 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0. Below that, exactly three of the fifteen output dwords move (+0x00, +0x10, +0x20) and nothing else in the struct does. EFFECT, measured end to end on THIS image (H 30 deg, V 30 deg, power 40%) at K=4.25 gain=0.3, standing unpressured kick, the game's OWN cleanliness factors, deviations drawn through its own type-4 randomiser 0x14401a060 with its real LCG and Box-Muller: ability 40 (f=0.00, S=0.700): ceilings h 11.94 / v 10.47 deg / p 32.2% vs STOCK h 4.20 / v 2.10 deg / p 28.8%; over a 20 m ball the p90 miss goes 120 -> 345 cm sideways and 56 -> 280 cm in weight/loft; ability 60 (f=0.10, S=0.730): ceilings h 11.17 / v 9.63 deg / p 31.9% vs STOCK h 4.20 / v 2.10 deg / p 28.8%; over a 20 m ball the p90 miss goes 115 -> 307 cm sideways and 51 -> 236 cm in weight/loft; ability 75 (f=0.50, S=0.850): ceilings h 8.07 / v 6.28 deg / p 30.5% vs STOCK h 4.20 / v 2.10 deg / p 28.8%; over a 20 m ball the p90 miss goes 85 -> 164 cm sideways and 35 -> 105 cm in weight/loft; ability 90 (f=0.90, S=0.970): ceilings h 4.97 / v 2.94 deg / p 29.2% vs STOCK h 4.20 / v 2.10 deg / p 28.8%; over a 20 m ball the p90 miss goes 59 -> 69 cm sideways and 25 -> 35 cm in weight/loft; ability 99 (f=1.00, S=1.000): ceilings h 4.20 / v 2.10 deg / p 28.8% vs STOCK h 4.20 / v 2.10 deg / p 28.8%; over a 20 m ball the p90 miss goes 56 -> 56 cm sideways and 23 -> 23 cm in weight/loft. WHY GAIN = 0.3: chosen against a rule that is not taste - the worst player's UNPRESSURED clean kick must stay BELOW what the stock game already gives that same player under light pressure, because a patch that makes standing still worse than being closed down reads as a bug rather than as a human error. The anchor is measured on this image by injecting the builder's own difficulty scalar D at 0x14401c1fc: a stock ability-40 player at D = 0.25 has a p90 miss of 286 cm sideways / 139 cm in weight over a 20 m ball, against 121 / 56 cm unpressured in stock. Measured unpressured p90 for that same player by gain: 0.05 -> 158 / 93 cm; 0.06 -> 165 / 100 cm; 0.08 -> 180 / 115 cm; 0.10 -> 195 / 130 cm; 0.12 -> 210 / 145 cm; 0.15 -> 233 / 167 cm; 0.20 -> 270 / 204 cm; 0.35 -> 384 / 317 cm. The chosen 0.3 is the largest value on that sweep that stays inside the anchor on BOTH axes; 0.12 and above break it. Be aware the vertical margin at the default is thin - not measured against a 139 cm anchor - so treat the default as the TOP of the sensible range, not the middle, and drop to 0.08 or 0.06 for headroom. An earlier revision of this spec shipped 0.35, chosen against a stock column that was wrongly believed to be zero; on this sweep 0.35 puts an unpressured 40-rated player further off line than the stock game's own HALF-pressure error for him. ALL cm figures in this spec are Monte-Carlo estimates from a few hundred to a few thousand draws - treat them as +-5%, and do not read a 5 cm difference between two of them as real INTERACTIONS - read before applying: (1) this spec OCCUPIES 0x14401b3a7 and materialises K itself, so it is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with error-sigma.json, cave-fatigue.json, cave-fatigue-weakfoot.json, loose-realism-v2.json and slices-scuffs*.json; exe_patch refuses the second one on the expect bytes. With the default K=4.25 (the stock value) applying this spec does NOT change sigma; regenerate with --k 6 to bundle error-sigma.json's change. (2) the flat per-kick-class multiplier at 0x14401be1e (x0.90 class 0, x0.88 class 1, x0.86 classes 2/3, x1.00 class 4; 57/46/34/35/4 of kick ids 1..0xb0) is ABILITY-INDEPENDENT and sits on the horizontal factor. The cave multiplies AFTER it, so the patched horizontal ceiling is (1 - c1_class*S)*30 deg - and because c2/c3 are derived from c1, that class term is already baked into the vertical and power ceilings as well. No class is exempt. (3) BEHAVIOUR CHANGE TO AGREE TO: the forced-horizontally-exact predicate 0x143edf000 (bit 17 of [player+0xad8] set AND [player+0x362d]&8 clear) sets c1 = 1.0 and the horizontal sigma factor to 1.0 at 0x14401b34a, BEFORE the hook, so those kicks are exactly straight in stock. The cave multiplies c1 after that and REMOVES that guarantee. WHAT SETS THAT BIT IS NOT KNOWN - a scripted, cutscene or set-piece kick are all live possibilities. Measured cost at gain 0.10 (S14a): ability 40 goes from exactly 0.0 to a p90 of 28 cm over 20 m (16 cm at a penalty's 11 m; worst observed 57 cm over 20 m), ability 75 to 14 cm, ability 99 unchanged. At the old gain 0.35 the same figures were 149 cm p90 and 275 cm worst case, which is a large part of why the gain came down. Regenerate with --axes vp to keep those kicks exact, at the cost of the sideways miss on every other kick. (4) the assisted-pass flag [player+0x362c]&1 still zeroes the HORIZONTAL deviation inside the randomiser at 0x14401a15d, whatever ceiling the builder produced; vertical and power are unaffected by it. Turn pass assistance OFF before concluding the patch does nothing. (5) technique-realism.json (APPLIED on the live exe) re-aims six difficulty thresholds; it does not touch this site and its expect bytes are unaffected. It also changed the ability weight B at 0x14401c1dc from 0.60 to 0.75 in c *= 1 - clamp01(0.1 + B*(1-f))*D, so it already made a bad player worse UNDER PRESSURE. Measured composition at ability 40 (p90 lateral / vertical cm over a 20 m ball): D=0 pristine 86/42, installed 86/56, installed + this cave at gain 0.10 139/130; D=0.25 188/91, 214/135, 259/206; D=1.00 524/240, 606/379, 615/430. The two terms multiply the same c and the ceiling saturates, so the cave's effect is concentrated exactly where it was aimed - the unpressured kick - and adds little on top of a heavily pressured one. (6) scuff-wobble.json entries 1+2 (APPLIED). Entry 1 raised the vertical ceiling 22.5 -> 30 deg at 0x14401b423, and every vertical number here is on that image (on pristine they would be 25% smaller). Entry 2, at 0x14401a12c, is recorded in this project as a 'vertical sign bias' and THAT LABEL IS WRONG: 0x14401a12c sits in the randomiser's FIRST block, which reads [rdi+0x10]/[rdi+0x14]/[rdi+0x48] - the slot the caller fills from kick-miss +0x00, i.e. the HORIZONTAL ceiling; it is the slot the assist flag kills and the one that is angle-wrapped into azimuth. Its 100 -> 50 change makes the AZIMUTH sign coin roughly 3:1 one-sided: measured over 1200 draws, 24% positive / 72% negative on the installed image versus 47% / 49% on pristine, with the elevation block identical on both. So the sideways error this cave opens up will DRAG ONE WAY rather than spray symmetrically, and linked-spin will curl it one way too. If that is not wanted the fix is at 0x14401a12c, not here. (7) linked-spin.json (APPLIED, hook 0x1440187b4, cave 0x14105ed1e - DIFFERENT padding, not disturbed): |added spin.y| = 0.5 rev/s per degree of horizontal miss, capped at 8 rev/s. Correcting an earlier claim in this spec: a stock clean kick does NOT produce zero horizontal miss, so linked-spin is already live on every kick. Measured at gain 0.10, mean added spin goes 0.63 -> 1.01 rev/s at ability 40 and 0.45 -> 0.59 at 75, and is unchanged at 0.30 for ability 99; worst cases 1.58 -> 2.54. All far inside the 8 rev/s cap, so the two compose without saturating. (8) shots (action id 0xa) that pass the 0x14401b379-b398 checks have c3 remapped to 0.25*c3 + 0.75 at 0x14401b39a BEFORE the hook, and all shots get their three sigma factors halved at 0x14401b338. The cave applies after both. WHERE THIS SITS IN THE EXE - it is NOT 'linker padding'. 0x1438b4835 is the empty body of the FOURTH 0x60-byte record of an anti-tamper trampoline pool starting at 0x1438b4710 (stride 0x60; records 1-3 at 0x1438b4710 / 0x1438b4770 / 0x1438b47d0 each open with a live 5-byte jmp into .impdata followed by 43-46 bytes of relocated branch data). The cave begins 5 bytes after record 4's own live 'jmp 0x15272c020', and .impdata carries characteristics 0x60000020 - CODE | EXECUTE | READ, i.e. the protector's own executable region. No unwind data covers that span. Nothing in the image references the run - no 64-bit pointer, no RVA, no direct branch, and both of the builder's indirect jumps are fully enumerated MSVC switch tables (0x14401b868/0x14401b878 and 0x14401b948/0x14401b954) whose targets all lie inside the builder - so the CORRECTNESS case is clean. It is the TAMPER-DETECTION case that is untested: writing 70 bytes into a live protector pool slot is a different bet from writing into ordinary alignment padding, and Denuvo's reaction to it is unknown. The 44-byte run at 0x1438b4804 is the tail of record 3 and carries exactly the same caveat. Per the backup metadata this same run was previously WRITTEN by the retired slice-cave-v2 / cave-axis-fix / test-spin specs; none of them is present now (the run is 91 clean int3 bytes on both the installed image and the pristine backup, checked here), and they must not be re-applied alongside this spec. The closest thing to real-world evidence either way is linked-spin.json: its own 85-byte cave at 0x14105ed1e sits in a region of the same character (an int3 run immediately after dense relocated branch data in .xcode) and is ALREADY APPLIED on this exe. If that build has been played without incident, that is a precedent for Denuvo tolerating bytes in these gaps - but it is the owner's observation to make, not something measured here. NOT PROVEN / EMULATION ONLY: (a) nothing at all has been observed in a running match; (b) the world these numbers come from is synthetic - a zeroed player object, with most object getters inside the factor functions stubbed - so the stock baseline is this harness's best reconstruction of a standing unpressured kick, not a capture from a real one; (c) every degree/cm figure is measured through the type-4 consumer 0x14401a060, which is what the builder selects by default (out+0x34 = 4 at 0x14401a937). Miss types 1 and 3 (set at 0x14401b5fd / 0x14401b7be) are consumed by 0x144019e40 instead, which reads the same three triples but applies its own formula and was NOT emulated: the mechanism covers them, the numbers do not; (d) struct+0x38 is a DETERMINISTIC floor, not a draw - the randomiser computes dev = ceil*(w + (1-w)*random) at 0x14401a115..0x14401a13d. Everything here is measured with w = 0, which is what the builder writes at 0x14401a991; only 0x14401e5b0 (called at 0x14401b5d5) can make it non-zero and whether it ever does in a real match is unknown. If it does, the cave multiplies a certainty rather than a probability - at w = 0.2 every 20 m pass from a 40-rated player would be at least ~70 cm off before any dice are rolled; (e) the D values quoted in (5) are injected at 0x14401c1fc, not reached naturally, and D's real scale is undecoded; (f) the ability -> f map is the game's own 0x143ed71d0 with the inner selector 0x143ed7440 stubbed to a chosen integer; the mapping from on-screen stats to that integer is taken from the existing docs, not re-derived here. ROLLBACK: python tools/exe_patch.py remove <this file>. IMPORTANT: exe_patch's remove compares the file against this spec's 'patch' bytes and aborts if they differ, so if you hand-edit the K or gain immediates at the addresses listed under tunables, remove will REFUSE - and the only tool left is restore, which reverts the exe to pristine and therefore also discards technique-realism, scuff-wobble and linked-spin. Change the gain by regenerating this spec (python tools/emu_kickerror.py --tiredness none --gain <g> --write-spec), not by editing bytes; if you have already hand-edited, edit the 'patch' hex in this JSON to match before running remove. Authored only - NOT applied, never run in-game.
status: authored, not applied, never run in-game. Mechanics proven by emulation (emu_kickerror.py --tiredness none: S1-S14 pass, exe_patch --dry-run passes). CALIBRATION REVISED after review: an earlier revision claimed the stock unpressured ceilings were zero and shipped gain 0.35 on that basis; both were wrong. The stock baseline is now measured with the factor functions executing (S11b) and the gain is derived from the game's own light-pressure error (S13). The one thing the owner must consciously accept is interaction (3), the forced-exact kicks.

K.meaning: Gaussian sigma scale in sigma = max(0.1, 0.75 + K*(1-s)^2). DEFAULT 4.25 = the STOCK value, so this cave does NOT bundle the sigma change. Setting it to 6.0 makes this spec include error-sigma.json's effect. Applies to EVERY kick.

gain.meaning: S = clamp01(1 - gain*(1 - f)), f = the ability factor. It is how much of the game's own remaining error headroom a 40-rated player (f = 0) gives up on a clean kick. Measured p90 miss for a 40-rated player on an unpressured 20 m ball, lateral / weight in cm: stock 121 / 56; 0.05 -> 158 / 93; 0.06 -> 165 / 100; 0.08 -> 180 / 115; 0.10 -> 195 / 130; 0.12 -> 210 / 145; 0.15 -> 233 / 167; 0.20 -> 270 / 204; 0.35 -> 384 / 317. The anchor the default is chosen against is 286 / 139 cm - what the stock game already gives the SAME player under light pressure (D = 0.25 injected at 0x14401c1fc). The default is the LARGEST value that stays inside it on both axes, so treat it as the top of the sensible range, not the middle. Values above 1 only saturate (S is floored at 0). CHANGE THIS BY REGENERATING THE SPEC (python tools/emu_kickerror.py --tiredness none --gain <g> --write-spec), not by editing these bytes - a hand-edit makes 'exe_patch remove' refuse (see ROLLBACK in the description).
